content.overview: Testamentary succession is disposition by will. For Hindus, HSA s. 30 enables disposition of property capable of testamentary disposition, including a male Hindu’s Mitakshara coparcenary interest; formalities are under the Indian Succession Act, 1925. For Muslims, classical rules generally limit bequests to one-third of the net estate to non-heirs without the consent of the heirs. Always separate intestate from testamentary succession.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Valid will? (2) Hindu or Muslim? (3) Capable property / one-third limit? (4) ISA formalities?
content.study:
Intestate rules apply only to property not validly disposed of by will.

Hindus: HSA s. 30 + ISA formalities; link to HSA s. 6 for coparcenary interest.

Muslims: generally one-third to non-heir without heirs’ consent; excess or bequests to heirs need consent as classical rules provide.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Intestate vs testamentary
sections.body: No valid will → intestate; valid will covering the property → testamentary.

sections.heading: Hindu power — HSA s. 30
sections.body: Any Hindu may dispose by will of capable property; male Mitakshara interest is deemed capable.

sections.heading: ISA formalities
sections.body: Sound disposing mind; execution and attestation (generally two witnesses for unprivileged wills); revocation rules; probate.

sections.heading: Muslim one-third rule
sections.body: Generally up to one-third of net estate to non-heir without heirs’ consent.

sections.heading: Residue
sections.body: Property not validly disposed of falls to the applicable intestate scheme.

examples.title: Self-acquired property
examples.body: Hindu executes a valid attested will of self-acquired house — will governs that house.

hypotheticals.question: No will — which regime?
hypotheticals.analysis: Intestate. For a Hindu male, ascertain interest under s. 6 then devolve under s. 8 (or other applicable intestate rules).

misconceptions.trap: A will automatically overrides all coparcenary rights without regard to HSA.
misconceptions.correction: Testamentary power over Mitakshara interest is recognised under HSA s. 30 and coordinated with s. 6.
